raw_response:
I farm only 3.5 mu, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on all of it instead of changing crops. That fits my land, my experience, and my family situation. Some people in my household work off-farm, so I will keep the plan simple, stable, and not too labor-intensive. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on that to protect yield in key periods rather than taking production risk. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put most of the fertilizer in as a base plus a topdressing at jointing, irrigate at the critical stages, and control weeds and diseases with limited but timely sprays. For maize, I will use hybrid seed for stronger yield, keep fertilizer balanced but nitrogen-led, irrigate when summer rain is not enough, and spray mainly for weeds and major insects or diseases if they show up. I will use rotary tillage because it saves labor and matches a small farm like mine. I am aiming for steady yield and manageable costs, not chasing the absolute maximum.
